# InputService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("InputService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Reads the state of the input devices and hosts the input action system. For gameplay input, use `InputAction`, which can be rebound and can show prompts; this service is for device state and for direct key and pointer reads.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GamepadAvailable` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether at least one gamepad is connected. It changes as gamepads are connected and disconnected. `InputDeviceChanged` fires when one is first used. |
| `KeyboardAvailable` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether a keyboard is attached. On a phone it is false until a keyboard is connected or paired. |
| `LastInputDeviceType` | `Enum.InputDeviceType` | — | read-only | The kind of device the player most recently used. Use it to switch a HUD's button prompts. It changes only on deliberate input: a gamepad stick resting inside its dead zone does not change it. |
| `PointerLocked` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether the pointer is locked to the window and reports movement instead of position, as a first-person camera needs. While it is locked, `GetPointerPosition` returns the position the pointer had when it was locked. To read the movement, bind a `Direction2D` action to `MouseMovement`.<br><br>While the pointer is locked, the interface ignores it: nothing is hovered or pressed, and no `Active` object receives it. The keyboard and a gamepad can still select UI objects. To let the player click the interface, unlock the pointer first, as a menu does. |
| `PointerVisible` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the system cursor is drawn. It is independent of `PointerLocked`: a strategy game can hide the cursor during a cutscene without locking it. |
| `PreferredGamepadId` | `number` | — | read-only | The connection id of the gamepad the player last used, or 0 if none is selected. A gamepad that reconnects gets a new id. The value is kept when the player switches to keyboard or touch. It is not a player index. |
| `PreferredGamepadType` | `Enum.GamepadType` | — | read-only | The family of the gamepad the player last used. Connecting a gamepad does not select it; the player must use it. The value is kept when the player switches to keyboard or touch, and becomes `Unknown` when that gamepad disconnects. Use it to choose button icons. |
| `PreferredInput` | `Enum.InputDeviceType` | — | read-only | The kind of input the player is using: `KeyboardMouse`, `Gamepad` or `Touch`. It has the same value as `LastInputDeviceType`, and `InputDeviceChanged` fires when it changes. For the family of the gamepad, use `PreferredGamepadType`. |
| `SwipeThreshold` | `number` | `6` | read/write | How far a finger must travel before the movement counts as a swipe, in millimeters on the screen. The default is 6. The engine converts it to pixels from the display's pixel density, so it is the same physical distance on a phone and on a monitor. |
| `TouchAvailable` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether this machine has a touchscreen. It is known from startup, before any touch, so a game can choose which HUD to build before its first frame. It is true on a phone and on a laptop with a touchscreen. |

## Methods

### `GetGamepads(): {number}`

Returns the ids of the connected gamepads, in ascending order. `GamepadConnected` and `GamepadDisconnected` fire when the list changes. Connecting a gamepad does not change `PreferredInput` or assign the gamepad to a local player.

### `GetPointerPosition(): Vector2`

Returns the position of the pointer in window pixels, measured from the top left, for the current tick. The value does not change within a tick.

### `IsGamepadKeyDown(gamepadId: number, keyCode: Enum.KeyCode): boolean`

Returns whether a key of one gamepad, given by its id, is held. It reads the device directly, whether or not the interface consumed the input. Returns false for a gamepad that is not connected and for a key that is not a gamepad key. An analog input counts as held beyond half of its range.

### `IsKeyDown(keyCode: Enum.KeyCode): boolean`

Returns whether a key, button or trigger is held, for the current tick. An analog input counts as held beyond half of its range.

It reads the device directly and ignores whether the interface consumed the input. For input that respects the interface and can be rebound, use an `InputAction`.

### `SetClipboard(text: string)`

Copies text to the player's clipboard, such as a room code, a seed or a link. The clipboard cannot be read: there is no method that returns its contents.

The text goes to the clipboard of the machine that runs the script, so call it from a client script. It does nothing on a server or in a headless run. The limit is 64 KiB; longer text is cut at a character boundary. If it is called several times in one frame, the last call is kept.

### `SetVirtualState(keyCode: Enum.KeyCode, value: number)`

Sets the value of one of the `Virtual` key codes from something that is not hardware. Use it for an on-screen button, an on-screen thumbstick or an accessibility control.

The value is treated like input from a device. It drives actions through an ordinary `InputBinding`, obeys context priority and `Sink`, and is recorded in a replay.

The value is a number, not a press. Use 1 and 0 for a button, and values in between for a slider or a thumbstick axis. A `Bool` action bound to it counts as pressed beyond 0.5.

The value stays until it is set again; it is cleared when the window loses focus. Raises an error for a key code that is not one of the `Virtual` codes.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `GamepadConnected(gamepadId: number, gamepadType: Enum.GamepadType)`

Fires when a gamepad connects. Connecting does not change `PreferredInput` or the preferred gamepad.

### `GamepadDisconnected(gamepadId: number, gamepadType: Enum.GamepadType)`

Fires when a gamepad disconnects. Passes the id it had and its family. Other connected gamepads are not affected.

### `InputBegan(input: InputObject, uiConsumed: boolean)`

Fires on the tick an input starts: a key or button is pressed, or a trigger passes half of its range.

The second argument, `uiConsumed`, is true when the interface already used the input, because the pointer was over a UI object or a `TextInput` had focus. Check it, or the game reacts to clicks on buttons and to text typed into a chat box.

A key handled through this event cannot be rebound by the player and does not appear in a settings menu. For gameplay input, an `InputAction` is usually the better choice; this event suits prototypes, debug keys and input that players never remap.

It fires on simulation ticks, so a handler that changes the world is reproduced exactly in a replay. For camera look at the frame rate, use an `InputContext` with `Rate` set to `Enum.InputRate.Render`.

### `InputChanged(input: InputObject, uiConsumed: boolean)`

Fires on a tick in which an input changed without starting or ending: the pointer moved, the wheel turned, or a stick or trigger changed position. `Position` and `Delta` hold the change.

It fires at most once per tick for each source, with the deltas accumulated since the previous event, so fast movement is not lost. As with `InputBegan`, input handled here cannot be rebound by the player.

### `InputDeviceChanged(deviceType: Enum.InputDeviceType)`

Fires when `LastInputDeviceType` changes. Use it to redraw button prompts.

### `InputEnded(input: InputObject, uiConsumed: boolean)`

Fires on the tick an input stops. It fires for every held input when the window loses focus, so a handler that pairs it with `InputBegan` never leaves an input stuck.

`uiConsumed` has the value it had when the input began, so a press that started on a button is still marked as consumed when it is released elsewhere.

### `PreferredGamepadIdChanged(gamepadId: number)`

Fires when `PreferredGamepadId` changes, including when the player switches between two gamepads of the same family.

### `PreferredGamepadTypeChanged(gamepadType: Enum.GamepadType)`

Fires when `PreferredGamepadType` changes. It is independent of `InputDeviceChanged`.

### `TouchLongPressed(position: Vector2)`

Fires once when a finger has stayed where it touched for half a second, while it is still down. Lifting the finger afterward does not count as a tap.

### `TouchPanned(delta: Vector2, fingers: number)`

Fires when the fingers that are down move. Passes how far they moved in this tick, in window pixels, as a single motion however many fingers there are; +Y is down the window, as for `Position`. Use it for a camera that is dragged with one finger or two.

### `TouchPinched(scale: number, center: Vector2)`

Fires on each tick in which two fingers move apart or together. Passes the distance between them relative to the distance when the second finger touched, so 2 means twice as far apart, and the point midway between them. To zoom, multiply the zoom the game had before the pinch by this ratio.

### `TouchSwiped(direction: Enum.SwipeDirection, start: Vector2, fingers: number)`

Fires when a finger, or the mouse with its left button held, travels `SwipeThreshold` along one axis. It fires while the finger is still down, with the position where the stroke began, in window pixels, and the number of fingers down.

One long drag in one direction is one swipe. A change of direction starts the next, measured from the finger's position at that moment. The same swipe also drives `Enum.KeyCode.SwipeUp` and its three siblings for an `InputAction`. A press that the interface consumed (see `UIObject.Active`) starts no touch gesture.

### `TouchTapped(position: Vector2)`

Fires when a finger touches and lifts at the same place within a third of a second. Passes the position, in window pixels. A mouse click on the world also fires it.

### `WindowFocusChanged(focused: boolean)`

Fires when the game window gains or loses keyboard focus. Losing focus releases every held input.
